title: Payment SDKs, Tokenization, and Tap-to-pay Boundaries Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies payment sdks, tokenization, and tap-to-pay boundaries?
options: Keep payment authority and cryptographic verification on trusted backend or certified components, with durable idempotent recovery.
questions.answer: Keep payment authority and cryptographic verification on trusted backend or certified components, with durable idempotent recovery.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: Receiving a Google Pay PaymentData callback means the merchant has successfully captured funds.
questions.explanation: Showing “paid” immediately after the client receives payment data can create false success when backend authorization times out or fails.

questions.prompt: Why must the backend reprice the cart?
questions.answer: Client amount and cart data can be stale or tampered; the trusted authority must validate the transaction before authorization.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
